evidence: Cic. Off. 1.92: vīvere simpliciter, fidēliter (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 33.35.9: cōnstanter et fidēliter in amīcitiā … permanēre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of loyalty to friends and to one’s word, and of doing a task honestly and well: memory that holds a thing faithfully, an art faithfully learnt.

evidence: Cic. Cael. 14: firmus amīcus ac fidēlis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The adjective, of friends, allies, servants, dogs; fīdus is the same in sense, more often in verse (Lewis & Short).
The adverb of fīdus occurs perhaps only in the superlative (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est. ejus duplex virtūs, facile percipere et fidēliter continēre
phrases.english: in little ones the chief sign of talent is memory; its strength is twofold, to take things in easily and to keep them faithfully

phrases.latin: adde quod ingenuās didicisse fidēliter artēs ēmollit mōrēs nec sinit esse ferōs
phrases.english: besides, to have faithfully learnt the liberal arts softens the character and does not let it be wild

sources: Lewis & Short: fidelis · Lewis & Short: fidus
